teams.heading: Hosting Ireland in Suva would be 'nothing greater' for Fiji
teams.body: Build-up coverage puts a Suva fixture above all else, though it does not say who made the remark. The idea is a pointed one given the summer Fiji have had: their Nations Championship "home" games were played on UK soil because of commercial considerations, with the national stadium not considered of a suitable standard to host regular Test matches. Fiji go into Saturday's trip to Dublin having lost 54-17 to France in Lyon.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item about Fiji on the shortlist, and it gives the fan a Fiji-side talking point rather than Ireland's selection.

teams.heading: Max Ojomoh recalled at 12 as Steve Borthwick reinstates him for Japan
teams.body: Bath centre Max Ojomoh is back in England's plans after being initially left out of England head coach Steve Borthwick's training squad, and returns at 12. He has not played for England since man-of-the-match against Argentina a year ago. Borthwick wants more than skill from the position: "You have to be incredibly skilled in that position, but it demands a skill and toughness it previously probably didn't," he told BBC Sport. Ojomoh partners George Ford, who returns to fly-half, with Henry Pollock starting too.

lead.why: A fresh England selection story with a named recall, ranked above the Itoje piece already reported and the Monye column.

teams.heading: Antoine Dupont inspires France past Springboks 21-19, ending five-match losing run
teams.body: France held on for a 21-19 win over South Africa at Stade de France, ending a five-match losing run against the world champions. Tries from Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Theo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey came in a frantic first half, and Antoine Dupont was named player of the match. South Africa number eight Jasper Wiese was shown a red card early in the second half, and Manie Libbok then missed the conversion that would have levelled the game. The win leaves France six points clear in the northern hemisphere standings.

lead.why: A fresh result, the first France win over South Africa in five meetings, and the strongest new France item on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Tadhg Beirne named Ireland captain as Andy Farrell makes seven changes
teams.body: Andy Farrell has made seven changes for Saturday's meeting with Fiji at the Aviva Stadium, with lock Tadhg Beirne captaining Ireland in a home game for the first time. Mack Hansen moves to fullback, Hugo Keenan drops out of the matchday 23, and Jamie Osborne and Bundee Aki form an all-new centre partnership. Dan Sheehan is stood down for 12 days with concussion, so Rónan Kelleher comes into the front row, and James McNabney is set to debut from the bench.

teams.heading: Giacomo Nicotera says Italy's self-review after 7-66 Springboks defeat was harsh
teams.body: Italy captain Giacomo Nicotera said the squad had been very critical after the 7-66 defeat to South Africa, reviewing aerial play, defence, organisation and discipline. Too many penalties, partly driven by South Africa's breakdown pressure, were something Italy can and must control. The Monday review was tough, Nicotera said, with players pushing each other for a sharper response in training. Ahead of Saturday's fifth-round Nations Championship test against Argentina, winning enough ball was fundamental, he added.

lead.why: Italy's captain's new post-Springboks self-assessment is fresh, Italy-specific team news ahead of the Argentina test, and the other shortlist items are either already reported or less pressing.

teams.heading: Graham and Kinghorn return as Townsend keeps pack unchanged for Australia
teams.body: Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend has restored Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn to his starting XV for the Test against Australia at Murrayfield. Kinghorn takes over at full-back from Kyle Rowe, who is not in the squad, while Graham returns on the left wing as Jamie Dobie drops to the bench. Graham, Scotland's all-time leading try scorer, recovered from a bicep tear more quickly than expected. The starting pack is unchanged and back-row Ollie Leatherbarrow could earn a first cap from the bench.

lead.why: It is a fresh selection event for Scotland's next Test, separate from the individual-responsibility comments already run.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy makes four changes, Taine Basham coming in at No. 8
teams.body: Planet Rugby reports that Taine Basham comes in at number eight, James Botham at blindside flank, Adam Beard at lock and Gabriel Hamer-Webb on the left wing for Saturday's Nations Championship test against New Zealand at the Principality Stadium. The changes follow a 28-21 win over Japan in which, as Planet Rugby puts it, Wales had to dig deep and their overall performance left a lot to be desired. BBC Sport adds that number eight Aaron Wainwright will be missed against New Zealand because of injury.

lead.why: It is a new team-selection story about Wales's own starting XV, which outranks the already-read Beard and Adams stories and the pundit and fan pieces.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi says winning matters, but Pumas need stability first against Italy
teams.body: Under heavy criticism after defeats to Scotland and England, Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi used his pre-match press conference to accept that results count but argue they must come from a process. For him, the route to victory is doing the basics to the highest standard all week, the only part the team controls, rather than chasing a result at all costs. Argentina's only win this calendar year came against Wales, and Italy is the next test of that approach.

lead.why: It is a fresh coach press-conference item about Argentina under pressure, and it is not a rehash of the captaincy news already reported.

teams.heading: Les Kiss recalls Carter Gordon at flyhalf as Declan Meredith is dropped
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss has restored Carter Gordon and Rob Valetini to the starting XV for Sunday's Nations Championship match against Scotland at Murrayfield. Gordon is back from a broken leg, and Kiss said: "Certainly Carter was the incumbent, so he was in a position of strength before he got injured." Declan Meredith has been dropped from the match-day 23. Australia have used seven different starting flyhalves since the last World Cup.

lead.why: Fresh selection news from Australia's own camp, which the other items on the shortlist do not offer.

teams.heading: Borthwick names Max Ojomoh and Henry Pollock in England side for Japan
teams.body: Ten personnel changes and two positional switches mark England head coach Steve Borthwick's team for Saturday's Twickenham fixture with Japan. Centre Max Ojomoh returns after his man-of-the-match display against Argentina a year ago, and Henry Pollock starts after scoring two tries from the wing against Australia. Japan, who have never beaten England in six attempts and sit 10th of 12 on the log, face a side reshaped for this test.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett named All Blacks captain for Wales, with Scott Barrett overlooked
teams.body: Beauden Barrett takes over the captaincy for Saturday's Test against Wales in Cardiff, the first time the 148-Test utility back has skippered New Zealand, replacing tour captain Codie Taylor. Head coach Dave Rennie chose his older brother over lock Scott Barrett, saying: "I don't think he needs the extra responsibility." Scott, New Zealand's first-choice captain in 2024 and 2025, starts at lock, and Rennie has not ruled out a future return to the captaincy.

lead.why: It is a fresh New Zealand selection call on the captaincy, which is a new item and a different story from the Morgan quote already run.

teams.heading: Erasmus blames Springboks' own errors, not referee Piardi, for Paris defeat
teams.body: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus stopped short of criticising referee Andrea Piardi after the two-point defeat in Paris on Friday night, spending much of his press conference on the pressure a referee faces before a partisan crowd. "I'm not blaming the ref," he said. Erasmus conceded the Boks may have asked too much of Piardi at scrum time, but put the blame on his own side: the team had played itself into a hole. He also said the coaching staff must answer for a tentative performance.

lead.why: It is a fresh post-match press conference from Erasmus on the Paris defeat, and it is not the front-row story already reported.
